analysis.title: Global Macro Chart of the Day (#193): Stress-testing the outlook: oil, yields and AI
key_insights: UBS's Global Markets Outlook models four alternative scenarios: oil at $60/bbl, oil at $150/bbl, US Treasury yields rising to 6.5% with other bond markets following, and AI disappointment.

The oil scenarios are asymmetric. Cheaper oil adds little to growth, while expensive oil removes a lot. Central banks react more forcefully to rising inflation than to falling inflation, and cuts take longer to work through.

$150/bbl oil now does about half the growth damage UBS estimated in March. The price rise is now spread over 2026-27 instead of one year, which means less inflation and less erosion of real disposable income.

The bond-yield scenario kept correcting itself. Central banks responded to weakness fast enough that yields would not stay at 6.5%, so UBS assumed some inflation stickiness to slow the policy response.

AI disappointment is the most damaging scenario. It assumes an exogenous 25% equity market correction, equal to a drop in household equity wealth of 60% of GDP, on par with the GFC and the dot-com bust (the equity market is now 2x as large).

In the AI scenario, weaker US consumption hits hyperscalers' revenue and free cash flow, which cuts AI capex further. Global growth falls by roughly 1pp in 2027 and 2028 versus baseline, and 12 economies enter recession.
In the AI scenario, unemployment rises by 1.3pp over two years, EUR/USD returns to 1.20, gold reaches $7,000, and several central banks cut to the zero lower bound.
